significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) predictive coupling: across outcome-matched scientific tasks, a higher "Route-Separability Score" predicts greater within-route than across-route intervention transfer. This would establish both a phenomenon—distinct routes to the same scalar remain representationally separable—and a limited mechanism-level functional link, constraining which models and outcomes should support route-specific interventions; that is materially stronger than the concept decodability studied in work such as Vig et al.'s BERTology Meets Biology, while avoiding the inference from probe accuracy alone cautioned against by Hewitt and Liang's control-task analysis. Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: failure of the coupling would invalidate route separability as evidence of functional mechanistic understanding, although failure of separability would only support route collapse for the covered outcomes and models. In the topic-substitution check, generic inquiry into scientific representations would not merit this score; the increment comes specifically from the many-to-one, outcome-matched setup and its predicted coupling to intervention transfer.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Route-Separability Score," presented as a "read-only diagnostic" that can screen whether a model distinguishes causal routes despite matched outputs; because it predicts later intervention generalization, it is ex ante relative to choosing or trusting route-specific edits rather than merely explaining an observed failure afterward. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive claim still predicts a relation—higher RSS should imply stronger within-route versus across-route transfer—rather than merely supplying a procedure for finding an arbitrary direction. The asserted scope spans protein, molecular, and materials models and multiple outcomes, with model researchers and scientific-model auditors downstream, although the admission that findings are "outcome- and model-specific" and the absence of a decision threshold limit deployment reach. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: removing RSS and its forward-looking transfer coupling leaves only the broad scientific-representation topic, not a transferable audit handle.
